question: True or false: a gas measured at a negative temperature on the kelvin scale is colder than absolute zero?
answer: False. It is hotter than any positive temperature. Temperature measures how disorder changes with added energy; when energy has a ceiling and most particles crowd near it, adding more makes the system tidier, and the temperature comes out negative. Such a potassium gas, made in Munich in 2013, would give heat to anything it touched.
move: Before trusting a minus sign, ask what the scale is built from.
trap: Reading the minus sign as below zero, as on a thermometer.
reference: Braun, Ronzheimer, Schreiber, Hodgman, Rom, Bloch & Schneider, Negative Absolute Temperature for Motional Degrees of Freedom, Science, 2013
